cards.text: In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, a new king takes the throne in Judah: Hezekiah son of Ahaz. He's twenty-five years old, and his mother is Abi, the daughter of Zechariah. Pull up a stool, friend, because every king in this book gets a verdict from the writer, and we're about to hear this one's.

cards.question: Every king needs a home base. Where does Hezekiah, the new king of Judah, reign?

cards.text: He'll reign there twenty-nine years. TWENTY-NINE! Friend, I've owned aprons that didn't last twenty-nine weeks.

cards.question: True or false: King Hezekiah does what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Just like his father David had done. And Hezekiah gets right to work: he removes the high places, shatters the sacred pillars, and then turns to the Asherah poles.

cards.question: King Hezekiah has removed the high places and shattered the sacred pillars. What does he do to the Asherah poles?

cards.text: Then there's a bronze snake called Nehushtan, the one Moses made back in the wilderness (Numbers 21:9). I know a thing or two about being old and kept around, friend, but this snake makes the expired coupon I shared a drawer with look BRAND new.

cards.question: What does King Hezekiah do with Nehushtan, the bronze snake Moses made?

answers.text: He puts it in the temple

cards.question: Hezekiah demolishes the bronze snake Moses made. Why?

answers.text: People had been burning incense to it
It had cracked beyond any repair
The king of Assyria wanted it

cards.text: Here's the heart of it: "Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel." Then the writer stops and lines him up next to the other kings of Judah.

cards.question: True or false: No king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before him or after him.
Hezekiah stays faithful and doesn't turn from following the LORD. He keeps the commandments the LORD had given ___.

cards.text: "And the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went." Then he makes a BOLD move when it comes to the king of Assyria.

cards.question: Hezekiah rebels against the king of Assyria. What does he refuse to do?
Hezekiah is on a ROLL. Which people does he defeat as far as Gaza, from watchtower to fortified city?

cards.text: Meanwhile, over in Israel. In Hezekiah's fourth year, which is Hoshea's seventh, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marches against Samaria and besieges it.

cards.question: Samaria is under siege by the Assyrians. How long until they capture it?
Samaria has fallen. Where does the king of Assyria send the Israelites?
Why does all this happen to the Israelites?

answers.text: They would not listen to the LORD or obey
Their city walls were built too low
Their army was too small to fight back

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this king's story is only getting started.

findings.problem: "Every king in this book gets a verdict from the writer" is a Bible fact with no reference. It also isn't strictly true, since not every king in Kings gets an evaluation (for example, Shallum in 2 Kings 15:13-15).

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The claim that every king gets a verdict overstates what the text shows. What Papa Dorin points out must be true.

rule.text: **Noticing.** What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: "Why does all this happen to the Israelites?" points back with "all this" to cards the baker can no longer see. The question should say what happened, for example that Samaria is captured and the Israelites are exiled to Assyria.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 10 of the 13 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Only cards 3 and 7 carry real jokes. Cards 1, 10, 13, 16 and 20 read as pleasant storytelling with no laugh, and moments like the three-year siege or the king's long reign could hold a bigger laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: **But he is FUNNY.** Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
